01.r: Nehemiah weighs the matter inwardly before he acts.
01.n: This form of the verb occurs only here; the brief's lexicon gives 'to consider', BDB 'counsel, advise'. Gesenius's main entry is the like-spelled verb 'to reign, to be king', and he notes that in Syriac and Chaldee the root means to consult; YLT's 'my heart reigneth over me' takes the 'reign' sense. Hebrew puts the verb first: 'and took counsel my heart'; our English puts the subject first.

02.r: Nehemiah's mind and will, the seat of his thinking.
02.n: The brief's lexicon puts mind, will and understanding among the senses of 'heart'. The KJV, JPS and ASV fold it into 'I consulted with myself'.

03.r: The deliberation is inward, within himself.
03.n: Literally 'upon me'. Hebrew uses this preposition for what goes on inside a person, so 'within me' is the closest English.

04.r: He takes the nobles to task, as one bringing a case.
04.n: Gesenius: TO CONTEND, TO STRIVE; the brief's lexicon also gives to conduct a case and to make complaint. The verb is in a lengthened form (an extra -ah ending) that does not change its meaning.

05.r: The nobles are the other party to the dispute.

06.r: The men of high birth among the people.
06.n: Gesenius: noble, freeborn, only in the plural. YLT's 'freemen' takes the 'freeborn' sense.

08.r: Officials who governed the people of Jerusalem.
08.n: Gesenius: properly a substitute, a deputy of a prince, hence a prefect, and used of the chiefs and rulers of the people of Jerusalem in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah, citing this verse. BDB distinguishes them from the nobles.

09.n: Like 'contended', it is in the lengthened form with an extra -ah ending.

11.r: A creditor's claim on a loan, with the gain it brings him.
11.n: A third word for gain from a loan, different from 'interest' and 'increase' in the laws on this page, so our English gives it 'usury' to keep it apart. Gesenius: usury, from the root נָשָׁא, citing this verse; BDB: lending on interest, or usury; STEPBible's lexicon adds that in Nehemiah 5:11 the rate was only one per cent. Geneva's 'burthens' and the JPS's 'upon pledge' read the word differently.

12.r: Every one of them, without exception.
12.n: The word for 'man' used in the sense 'each'.

13.r: Their own fellow Jews are the ones the usury is exacted from.
13.n: Literally 'in his brother' or 'on his brother'; with this verb the preposition marks the person the claim is made against, so English says 'from'. 'Brother' here means a fellow Jew.

14.r: The nobles and officials, addressed directly.
14.n: The pronoun is written out, which makes the charge pointed: 'you are the ones'.

15.r: They are pressing their own people for usury, as creditors.
15.n: A participle, 'you are exacting', an action still going on. STEPBible files it under a verb whose Gesenius entry, printed in the brief, is 'to take up, to lift up', and glosses it 'lending'; we take it as the creditor's verb of Nehemiah 5:11 on this page and render it 'exact', keeping 'lend' for a different verb (Exodus 22:25 on this page). The noun 'usury' at the head of the clause is written with the same letters, so noun and verb echo each other.

16.r: He convenes an assembly to deal with them.
16.n: The ordinary verb 'to give, put, set'.

17.r: The assembly is called to face the nobles and officials.

18.r: A public meeting of the people.
18.n: Gesenius: an assembly, citing this verse. The brief's lexicon says the word occurs in only two verses.

19.n: The brief's short lexicon entry here belongs to a different word (heap, wave); Gesenius's entry, 'great', is the right one.

01.n: βουλεύω, to take counsel, deliberate. Swete's text numbers this book 2 Esdras.

03.n: ἐπʼ ἐμέ, 'upon me', exactly the Hebrew phrase.

04.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. ἐμαχεσάμην, 'I fought, I quarrelled'.

09.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. εἶπα, 'I said'.

11.n: The brief takes this word as the verb ἀπαιτέω, to demand back, 'he will demand'. It may instead be the noun ἀπαίτησις, a demand, in the dative, answering the Hebrew noun; we cannot settle it from the brief and leave the form as given.

15.n: ἀπαιτέω, to demand back, to ask for repayment: the Greek sees the lenders pressing for payment.

18.n: ἐκκλησία, an assembly, the word the New Testament uses for the church.
